PullRequest.Title: sessions: hold the custom agents spotlight until 3 Agents window requests
PullRequest.Body:

## What

**Agents window: don't show the "Find your custom agents" spotlight to new users.** The Agents window spotlight now waits until the user has sent at least 3 requests from the Agents window. It reuses the existing Agents window request count that onboarding already gates on (`AgentsWindowUsage.createdSessionCount`, incremented for each request that starts a session). `AgentHostAgentPickerContribution` offers no eligible composer to the spotlight while the count is below 3. The editor window spotlight is unchanged.

**Track custom agent usage across both windows.** Nothing stored this before. `CustomAgentUsageContribution` is registered in `chat.shared.contribution.ts`, so it runs in both the editor window and the Agents window. Each time a request is submitted with a custom agent, it increments `chat.customAgentUsage.count` and records the timestamp in `chat.customAgentUsage.lastUsed`. Both use `APPLICATION_SHARED` / `MACHINE` storage, shared by all windows, profiles and the Agents app.

- `IChatRequestAcceptedEvent` now carries the submitted `modeInfo`, so every send path in both windows records from one listener. The listener registers at `BlockRestore` so early submissions are not missed (its harness dependency is created lazily).
- "Custom" uses the same definition as the spotlight. Built-in modes (Agent/Ask/Edit), agents of the built-in chat extension (e.g. Plan, but not organization agents) and `builtIn`-storage agents (e.g. Agent Host built-ins) are excluded. The agent's source is resolved through `ICustomizationHarnessService.getCustomAgents`, so local and Agent Host sessions are handled alike. Agent Host agents synced from VS Code carry their original location as the new optional `ICustomAgent.sourceUri`, so organization agents are recognized even though their `uri` is the synced copy. A non-built-in agent that cannot be resolved still counts, because the sender marked it as custom.

## Notes for reviewers

- The custom-agent counter is best effort, like `EditorChatUsage`: overlapping writes from concurrent windows can lose an increment.
- No telemetry events are added. This is local state only, for future onboarding decisions.

## How to test

1. With a fresh `agentSessions.telemetry.totalSessions` state and `chat.agentsPickerInAttachContextMenu` on, open the Agents window with a workspace that has a custom agent. The spotlight does not show until 3 sessions have been started.
2. In either window, send a request with a workspace `.agent.md` agent and check that `chat.customAgentUsage.count` / `chat.customAgentUsage.lastUsed` update in shared application storage. Sending with Agent or Plan does not change them.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` then `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/agentsWindowUsage.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/customAgentUsage.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentCustomizationItemProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/remoteAgentHostCustomizationHarness.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatService/chatService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostAgentPicker.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/onboarding/agentPickerSpotlight.test.ts`: 450 passing (also runs `agentCustomizationItemProvider.test.ts` and `remoteAgentHostCustomizationHarness.test.ts`)
- Not run: manual end-to-end verification in a running Agents window.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed event path, uncached Agent Host provider path, explicit extension-host proxy call, and per-request/queued multiplicity are all directly traced in repository code. Exact provider cost and number of affected users vary, so severity is medium rather than high; the repeated IPC mechanism itself is not speculative.
Findings.PerformanceResource: extension-host IPC calls, extension provider discovery work, and readonly-file update work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For Agent Host sessions, cost grows as accepted custom-agent requests × registered custom-agent providers; queued requests launch independent, overlapping enumerations because the listener discards the promise and has no cache or coalescing.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive IPC and extension-host/filesystem work, reducing extension-host throughput and responsiveness during repeated or queued Agent Host requests
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this contribution, accepting an Agent Host request did not resolve the complete custom-agent inventory. Agent metadata was enumerated only for consumers such as the picker/customization UI; request acceptance itself performed no provider-listing IPC for usage accounting.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each accepted non-builtin request with a mode URI now calls ICustomizationHarnessService.getCustomAgents. For Agent Host harnesses this invokes AgentCustomizationItemProvider.provideCustomAgents, whose getAgentSources calls listPromptFilesForStorage(extension) on every invocation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 33 newly invokes customizationHarnessService.getCustomAgents for every accepted non-builtin request with a URI; no request-acceptance listener performed this inventory/provider enumeration before the PR.
Findings.Title: Cache the selected agent’s provenance instead of re-enumerating providers on every send
Findings.Impact: Using a custom agent in an Agent Host session now causes a full extension-agent source resolution after every send. With one or more ChatCustomAgentProviders, each send activates the provider event and invokes every provider across the extension-host boundary; several queued sends can multiply that work concurrently even though only the selected agent’s built-in/custom classification is needed.
Findings.Evidence: The added call at line 33 reaches CustomizationHarnessServiceBase.getCustomAgents -> AgentCustomizationItemProvider.provideCustomAgents -> getAgentSources -> PromptsService.listPromptFilesForStorage(PromptsStorage.extension). ExtensionPromptFileService.getExtensionPromptFiles has no cache and _listFromProviders calls each provider's providePromptFiles sequentially; MainThreadChatAgents2 implements that call with this._proxy.$providePromptFiles, an extension-host IPC. The onDidAcceptRequest listener starts recordRequest without awaiting or coalescing it, so queued accepted requests can run separate passes concurrently. The normal local prompts-service path has CachedPromise, but the Agent Host item-provider path does not.
Findings.Recommendation: Record or retain the selected mode’s provenance when modes are produced and pass that classification with modeInfo, or cache classification by session/type and mode URI with invalidation from onDidChangeCustomAgents. At minimum, coalesce in-flight inventory resolution so queued sends share one provider enumeration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Submit a request with a custom agent in a local/editor chat session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatService already resolves PromptsService.getCustomAgents before accepting a local custom-mode request. The new usage listener runs asynchronously after onDidAcceptRequest and does not block request dispatch; its storage update occurs after classification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover and parse local/user/extension custom-agent files through PromptsService.getCustomAgents
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced cold pass over discovered agent files; warm accepted requests reuse CachedPromise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: ChatService.sendRequest already called PromptsService.getCustomAgents for a local mode URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already completes before a local custom-mode request is accepted; the added listener's repeated read is warm and off the request critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke registered ChatCustomAgentProviders through $providePromptFiles during cold discovery
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC per registered agent provider on a cold/invalidated discovery pass, coalesced by PromptsService CachedPromise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider enumeration was already required by local custom-agent validation before acceptance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can be on the existing local send path during cold discovery; the diff does not add another cold pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist custom-agent usage count and last-used timestamp in application-shared machine storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storeAll containing two keys per classified custom-agent request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No custom-agent usage state was stored.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs from the asynchronous listener after acceptance, so it is off request dispatch's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One classification and one two-key usage update per accepted custom-agent request; agent-array scanning scales with discovered agents, but the discovery result is cached and coalesced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: PromptsService CachedPromise shares the cold discovery pass and serves warm calls until file/config/provider invalidation. Separate accepted requests may run listener promises concurrently, but their agent discovery uses the same cache.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold discovery lists and parses agent files and may invoke extension providers; this was already on the local custom-mode send path before the diff. The new listener normally observes the just-populated CachedPromise. Warm reads allocate/filter the cached result; invalidation is event driven.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the pre-acceptance local discovery and CachedPromise ownership are explicit, as is the post-acceptance storage call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Storage backend flush timing and typical custom-agent request frequency are not established; the cached local discovery means no separate reportable local discovery regression was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. The newly added local classification normally reuses discovery already completed by the unchanged send path; the per-request storage write is bounded and required by the requested count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Submit one or several queued custom-agent requests in an Agent Host/Agents window session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The usage listener is fire-and-forget after request acceptance, so enumeration does not delay request dispatch directly. It consumes extension-host/IPC and provider resources shared with interactive work after every accepted custom-agent request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for the first Agent Host customization-state snapshot when the session subscription is not ready
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one shared readiness promise per session subscription; callers race it with their token.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Request acceptance did not query customization readiness for usage accounting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly reached by usage classification but off request dispatch's critical path; subsequent calls are resolved from state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate agent-provider extensions and call every registered provider through $providePromptFiles
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC per registered custom-agent provider per accepted Agent Host custom-agent request; Q queued requests can produce Q overlapping P-provider passes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent Host request acceptance did not enumerate extension custom-agent providers; enumeration occurred for picker/customization consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off direct request dispatch, but competes for the extension host and provider resources and can reduce responsiveness/throughput.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reapply readonly configuration to all extension-provider agent URIs after each provider listing
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched updateReadonly call per uncached inventory pass, with all provider-returned URIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No request-acceptance path triggered this update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget from the provider listing, but adds repeated filesystem/configuration work after every send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded two-key storeAll per request after classification succeeds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Accepted custom-agent requests multiplied by registered ChatCustomAgentProviders and returned extension agent files. Queued requests are accepted individually and each starts a separate enumeration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each inventory pass invokes providers serially, but the listener has no sequencer, limiter, cache, or in-flight coalescing, so separate accepted/queued requests can overlap entire passes. The first remote-state readiness wait is memoized per subscription, but source resolution after it is not.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Agent Host customization state is already materialized or shares a memoized readiness promise. However, AgentCustomizationItemProvider.getAgentSources calls listPromptFilesForStorage(extension) every time, and ExtensionPromptFileService provider results are uncached; warm sends therefore repeat all provider IPC.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the added line, Agent Host item-provider call chain, uncached provider loop, extension-host proxy, and independent listener promises are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number and cost of installed providers varies, and the work is post-acceptance rather than directly blocking the send. The uncached per-request IPC cardinality and overlap are certain, supporting medium severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium performance regression: repeated uncached provider enumeration and overlapping IPC are introduced solely to classify the selected agent.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new listener checks modeInfo and isBuiltin synchronously and returns before resolving agents or writing usage.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per accepted built-in request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous inventory or storage work is launched.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression beyond a negligible event callback and branch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Agents window and evaluate the custom-agent picker spotlight before and after three session-starting requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Spotlight eligibility synchronously reads a numeric storage value initially and when the specific session-count key changes; it suppresses later widget/session eligibility work while below the threshold.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the Agents Window created-session count through IStorageService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial read and one read per matching storage change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Spotlight eligibility did not consult this count and evaluated widget/session state immediately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous eligibility check on spotlight recomputation; below threshold it avoids the rest of the derived spotlight work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One storage read per initial observation or relevant count-change event; count threshold is fixed at three.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable event handling is serialized on storage changes; no new async fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the storage service as authoritative state and subscribes only to the count key. There is no expensive discovery cache involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the observable subscribes to one storage key and reads one number.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Storage service implementation details are not measured, but the read is scalar and event-filtered.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; work is bounded and also suppresses downstream spotlight evaluation for new users.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enumerate Agent Host custom agents for the picker/customization UI after sourceUri propagation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing provider path waits for customization readiness, resolves sources, and maps all agents before the UI receives them. The diff only retains an origin URI already computed in getAgentSources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Agent Host customization readiness and extension provider files for source labels
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing pass per provider invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same readiness and provider listing occurred; the computed origin URI was used for labels but not returned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing picker/customization enumeration path; sourceUri assignment does not add a boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing mapping and source-label work scale with the number of Agent Host agents; sourceUri adds one optional reference per returned agent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged: one provider invocation from the consumer; internal extension-provider listing remains serial within a pass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unchanged by sourceUri propagation. Existing source resolution is uncached, but the diff does not increase picker invocation frequency or add a new boundary on this scenario.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the changed mapping and pre-existing origins map.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent counts vary, but the diff's retained URI field is small and bounded by the already-returned agent list.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression from sourceUri propagation itself.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench BlockRestore startup with custom-agent usage tracking registered
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution registers one chat acceptance listener. ICustomizationHarnessService is registered as a delayed singleton, so constructing the contribution does not itself run agent discovery or provider IPC.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One contribution and one listener per window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No startup task is launched; work begins only on accepted requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No agent inventory is fetched at startup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from delayed singleton registration and constructor behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DI proxy overhead is implementation-specific but bounded and no discovery call is made.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and all diff hunks. One medium boundary-fanout regression was submitted for uncached extension-provider enumeration on every Agent Host custom-agent send. Local cached discovery, usage storage, spotlight gating, startup registration, and sourceUri propagation were inspected and did not independently meet the reporting threshold.
